title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff + load-shedding ordering during regional failover
author: Asha Kulkarni
description: Production incident (2026-02-19) exposed a race in the SLO enforcer where concurrent regional failover + aggressive backoff caused out-of-order load-shedding decisions and a short spike of error responses for a subset of customers. This hotfix addresses three related issues: 1) tighten the ordering guarantees in the enforcer's backoff queue so older backoff events cannot be preempted by newer regional failover signals; 2) add an idempotent upsert for per-route load-shedding thresholds to avoid transient double-shedding during rapid config reconciliation; 3) implement a short hysteresis window around regional failover handoff to allow in-flight requests to finish before aggressive shedding kicks in. The patch includes unit tests for ordering invariants, an e2e canary that simulates regional failover under load, and a staged rollout plan (canary -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on SLO regressions. Motivation and context: We observed that when a region's capacity dropped suddenly and the control plane triggered failover, the enforcer processed backoff events and failover events concurrently. Due to a small window in the event queue comparator, newer failover events could be handled before older backoff entries were applied, causing duplicated load-shedding and violating per-route SLOs. This caused an increase in 5xx for a subset of customers and triggered PagerDuty. The root cause is ordering and lack of idempotency in per-route threshold reconciliation. This change is backward-compatible (config surface unchanged) and scoped to the enforcer subsystem and the config reconciliation path. Hotfix notes: prioritized patch, tests, and rapid canary rollout. See linked Linear tickets for additional context.

release_notes: Hotfix: Stabilize SLO enforcer ordering and prevent duplicate load-shedding during regional failover. Fix preserves per-route SLOs and adds short hysteresis to reduce transient 5xx during handoff.
rollback_plan: If canary or 25% rollout shows SLO regressions: revert hotfix via emergency revert (revert PR queued) and scale up regional capacity; restore previous enforcer binary. Run postmortem and apply more conservative hysteresis configuration.
